column1: # One row per served image shape. A profile_id names a bundle in
# scripts/image-models.tsv at one placement arm and one request geometry, and
# several profiles reach one bundle the way several web profiles reach one
# checkpoint in scripts/web-profiles.tsv.
# placement names where each component executes: `A` puts the text encoder,
# the diffusion trunk, and the VAE on the device; `B` runs the text encoder on
# the CPU with diffusion and VAE on the device; `C` runs the text encoder and
# the VAE on the CPU with diffusion alone on the device. The device is CUDA0
# under a CUDA-native image runtime, which is the runtime a fresh admission on
# this host builds; the letters named Vulkan placements under the prior host's
# runtime and keep their meaning as component splits. The arm binds the bundle's own
# composition, so scripts/image-registry.sh requires arm B to name a text
# encoder and arm C to name a text encoder and a VAE -- a bundle that omits the
# component an arm places has no arm to place it on. That requirement is
# mechanism and stays current; which arm wins is a measured claim and does not.
# width, height, and steps are what the profile requests; max_dimension and
# max_steps are what it admits. The registry requires width and height at or
# below max_dimension and steps at or below max_steps, so an authorization
# grant that names a larger image is refused against the profile rather than
# against the runtime. timeout_s is the runtime's own hard bound, and the
# service, MCP, router, and browser deadlines stack above it so a stalled run
# is ended by the process that owns it.
# execution_policy decides what the profile may do, over `refused` and
# `validator-gated`, mirroring scripts/web-profiles.tsv. `refused` runs nothing:
# the profile is an admitted shape and no generation executes against it.
# `validator-gated` admits a generation behind an authorization grant that
# binds prompt hash, seed, dimensions, and step count, and it requires
# validated_evidence to name a retained record that exists in the tree, because
# a profile that may spend the device must carry the run that showed it safe.
# Every row here reads `refused`: no image row has run validator-gated on this
# host, and the legacy provenance section below states what moved a row there
# before and what a CUDA-host campaign must show to move one there again.
# validated_evidence is a repository-relative path, `-` where no run has been
# retained. Any path present must exist in the tree whatever the policy reads,
# so a record removed from the tree refuses the query rather than leaving a
# claim pointing at nothing. Every row here reads `-`.
# review_model pairs one vision checkpoint with this image shape, because the
# reviewer belongs to the profile that produced the artifact rather than to the
# conversation that asked for it. `-` offers no review, and every row here
# reads `-`. A named value would be a scripts/models.tsv model_id whose
# projector column reads `required`; scripts/build-web-presets.sh joins it
# against that registry, requires a projector on disk and a validated tuple
# with the projector loaded, and emits a review-only section beside the
# language one. That section carries the vision row's own tuple and its
# projector, names no MCP configuration, and offers no tool, so the page
# reviews an artifact through it and reaches nothing else.
# --- Legacy provenance: the prior Vulkan/APU admission campaign ---
# Every measured claim below was established on the prior qwen-apu host --
# an AMD Athlon Silver 3050U iGPU sharing one DDR4 controller between compute
# and system memory -- before the RTX 4070 Ti retarget. Commit 9c5142f, the
# prior-host isolation that established the NVIDIA authority checks, deleted the raw records from this tree along with the rest of that host's
# roughly 1300 evidence files; the authoritative copies remain in `qwen-apu`
# at commit 55d8c73268d8c6496e77baaad732e1aea7a6183b, reachable from this tree
# as the `apu-upstream` remote, per evidence/legacy/raven2/README.md.
# Which placement arm wins was measured there, not here: every tested hybrid
# placement lost to full Vulkan because the text encoder on the CPU and the
# diffusion trunk on Vulkan drew on that host's one shared DDR4 controller
# (evidence/image-appliance/design.md, prior-host reading). This device has no
# such sharing -- the diffusion trunk would occupy discrete GDDR6X and a
# CPU-placed component would cross PCIe to separate DDR4 -- so the arm-B/C
# penalty this reasoning predicts is itself unmeasured here.
# image-sdxs-512-a is the row that campaign moved to `validator-gated`, on two
# prior-host runs neither retained in this tree: an approved generation
# reaching router, broker, MCP child, and service (`served-turn-admission`,
# commit 00de5c3 on `apu-upstream`), and a paired review naming lfm25-vl-16b
# after that host's own budget gate admitted the pair at 4388 MiB against
# 11.42 GiB of Vulkan margin (`paired-review-admission`, commit 41059af on
# `apu-upstream`). Both margins are that host's 29 GiB UMA carve-out, not this
# one's 12282 MiB GDDR6X carve-out, so neither number bounds anything here.
# This repository's own `evidence/image-appliance/` retains the narrative
# design documents from that campaign (design.md, vision-review-design.md,
# vision-review-control-design.md, stable-diffusion-cpp-pin.md) because they
# state mechanism rather than a prior-host-specific rate; it retains none of the
# admission run records themselves, which is why every row here reads
# `refused` rather than citing them as current.
# --- Future CUDA admission gate ---
# A row returns to `validator-gated` on this host only after a campaign here
# establishes all four of the following, each as a retained record under
# evidence/image-appliance/ or a sibling this section can be extended to name:
#   1. A placement arm measured under a CUDA-native image runtime, with each
#      component's placement read off the runtime's own device accounting
#      (text encoder, diffusion trunk, and VAE each named on CUDA0 or on the
#      CPU), since the DDR4-sharing argument above does not transfer to a
#      discrete card and no arm has been run against a PCIe-separated
#      CPU/GPU split. A Vulkan-ICD arm proves nothing here: Vulkan serving
#      is retired on this host and the row would carry a new CUDA profile
#      identity rather than reinterpreting this one.
#   2. A device-memory budget probe against the 12282 MiB carve-out this host
#      actually carries, replacing the 4388-MiB-against-11.42-GiB prior-host UMA
#      figure with one measured against this carve-out and the resident LLM
#      row it must share the device with.
#   3. A served-turn record taken on this host: an approved generation
#      reaching router, broker, MCP child, and service the way
#      `served-turn-admission` did on the prior host, retained here rather than cited
#      from `apu-upstream`.
#   4. Re-validation of the review pairing on this host: the vision reviewer
#      named by review_model measured resident beside the image runtime under
#      this carve-out, with a fresh paired-review record standing in for
#      `paired-review-admission`.
# Until all four are retained here, execution_policy stays `refused` on every
# row and validated_evidence and review_model stay `-`.
